![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134863/assets/8d7ceac8c936a745ae79f71844a6d1a74175b1b97a2a497588d34c9ff988cdf9.png)

Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<3,\,\bbox[5px,border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}}\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134863/assets/c0e6ef400b15c54264a400af99bef64c3bb5aeb7ceadbdd599375c0f1e0d3642.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134863/assets/8c5bbdfca6736194791f834ab4aadb03a30e3f116e89ffd5a7ea3e0104708ae4.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<3,\,0<y<\frac{2}{3}x\}.
$$
